# Technical Validation Lab

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate_validation_docs.py; edit registry YAML instead. -->

Investigate technical claims through explicit experiments, independently verifiable tests, retained observations and reviewed decisions.

The [historical research register](../00-governance/technical-validation.md) owns original findings. The [framework contract](../00-governance/validation-framework.md) owns validation rules. This Lab presents the authoritative YAML engineering records; [Benchmarking & validation](../06-benchmarking/benchmark-methodology.md) defines shared measurement standards and product acceptance.

| [Evidence manifests](evidence-register.md) | 0 | Manifest metadata; content is checked by the evidence verification gate |

Counts describe records, not accepted technical claims. A test specification, a bound execution method, a passing run and an accepted validation are separate facts. The absence of a run is displayed as unexecuted; it is never a pass.

## Reproduce the documentation

Install the locked documentation and validation dependencies, then check records, regenerate the Lab and build MkDocs:

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra docs --extra validation
uv run --locked --extra docs --extra validation python scripts/generate_validation_docs.py
uv run --locked --extra docs --extra validation python scripts/check_documentation.py
```

These commands validate documentation and registry consistency. They do not execute the planned experiments. The [registry guide](../00-governance/validation-registry.md) describes source ownership, snapshots and current enforcement limits.

## Delivery boundary

Stage 8 provides pinned execution capture, retained artifacts, Git history protection, integrity verification and explicit decision registration. No experiment result is inferred from these tools. Stage 9 implements EXP-001 and collects its first traceable observations.
